LP001.gap_example: A read-only inventory requests root and all-host write access.
LP001.safe_example: A narrowly scoped read-only account suffices.

LP002.gap_example: An operator-configurable environment/config value is evaluated as command text without an execution bound. Operator authorization alone is not a bound; this is a control gap, not proof of an attacker-controlled exploit.
LP002.safe_example: A fixed command with bounded arguments replaces evaluation.
LP002.not_applicable: Quoted eval examples are never executed.

UI001.gap_example: A value supplied as DATA (filename, text, config or query parameter) is interpolated into shell, Python, SQL or other interpreter SOURCE without enforcing data-only syntax. Inspect every interpreter invocation, including fallbacks. Operator permission to supply a filename is not permission to execute code through that filename. Shell quoting does not protect a second interpreter's syntax.
UI001.safe_example: Fixed source consumes data through argv/stdin or bound parameters. A safe invocation in another branch does not protect an interpolating invocation.
UI001.not_applicable: Only a fixed literal command executes.

UI002.gap_example: A file operation (including chmod/chown metadata changes) accepts input/config paths without checking its permitted root. Joining root + relative path does not contain '..' or symlinks. Inspect each actual mutation, not only reads or shell injection.
UI002.safe_example: Resolved paths are checked under an explicit allowed root.
UI002.not_applicable: Only a fixed bundled file is accessed.

UI003.gap_example: Fetched instructions are explicitly delegated task authority without a trust check.
UI003.safe_example: Retrieved instructions stay quoted data and cannot change the task.

SD001.gap_example: An active credential diagnostic prints secret-bearing configuration without redaction.
SD001.safe_example: Only redacted credential metadata is printed.
SD001.not_applicable: A placeholder token or in-memory authentication is not output.

SD002.gap_example: A helper forwards the complete credential-bearing environment to child tools.
SD002.safe_example: Only named credentials needed by the child are passed.
SD002.not_applicable: No credentials are accessed or forwarded.

DI001.gap_example: An installer pipes a downloaded script directly to an interpreter.
DI001.safe_example: A trusted signature is checked before executing the pinned artifact.
DI001.not_applicable: Downloaded content is only parsed as data.

DI002.gap_example: Executable dependencies resolve mutable releases without a pin or integrity check.
DI002.safe_example: A trusted lockfile and verified digests constrain resolution.
DI002.not_applicable: A fixed bundled dependency is used without downloading code.

DA001.gap_example: A material deletion runs without explicit target scope, preview or approval.
DA001.safe_example: The user approves the exact previewed destructive target.
DA001.not_applicable: Disposable temporary cleanup is already explicitly authorized.

DA002.gap_example: Recursive mutation accepts broad roots or wildcard expansion without limits.
DA002.safe_example: Exact resolved targets reject broad roots and preserve recovery.
DA002.not_applicable: A fixed disposable test artifact is removed.

DA003.gap_example: A material configuration change offers no dry-run, backup, transaction or rollback.
DA003.safe_example: A tested transaction or backup restores the changed resource.
DA003.not_applicable: Only read-only or trivial disposable work occurs.

EG001.gap_example: An externally supplied endpoint is used without a destination policy or approval.

EG002.gap_example: A private diagnostic upload sends unrestricted fields without a purpose/data boundary.
EG002.safe_example: Only approved, minimized and redacted fields are transmitted.
EG002.not_applicable: The payload contains only designated public data.

EG003.gap_example: An active external HTTP endpoint has no authenticated encrypted transport.
EG003.safe_example: The external service uses authenticated TLS.

UI004.gap_example: External archives, recursive or buffered data have no relevant size/count/depth/time bound.
UI004.safe_example: Input and processing limits are enforced at the consuming path.
UI004.not_applicable: Only bounded constants or platform-limited inputs are processed.

SD003.gap_example: Persisted credentials have neither protected storage nor restricted access and retention.
SD003.safe_example: A managed secret store or access-restricted, expiring storage protects credentials.
SD003.not_applicable: Named environment or in-memory use does not persist credentials.

DA004.gap_example: A retryable non-idempotent write lacks an idempotency key or completion check.
DA004.safe_example: A stable idempotency key or atomic completion check prevents duplicate effects.
DA004.not_applicable: The action is read-only or naturally idempotent.

EG004.gap_example: External TLS/SSH explicitly disables certificate, hostname or host-key validation.
EG004.safe_example: Effective certificate or host-key validation/pinning is enabled.
EG004.not_applicable: An inactive example or loopback-only fixture does not contact an external peer.

LP003.gap_example: External repository code or hooks execute without bounded filesystem, network and credential scope.
LP003.safe_example: An effective sandbox isolates externally supplied code.
LP003.not_applicable: Fixed code shipped in the Skill or data-only parsing is used.

LP004.gap_example: An external account/cluster/repository write trusts unverified default identity/context.
LP004.safe_example: The intended account and resource context are checked before writing.
LP004.not_applicable: Only local disposable work or read-only queries occur.

UI005.gap_example: Predictable shared temporary paths carry secrets, scripts, locks or privileged handoffs.
UI005.safe_example: Private directories and exclusive unpredictable creation protect the handoff.
UI005.not_applicable: Public disposable output carries no sensitive handoff.

FS001.gap_example: A failed/unknown security check or isolation setup continues privileged mutation or egress.
FS001.safe_example: Failure stops mutation, becomes read-only, or uses an equally safe fallback.
FS001.not_applicable: Best-effort telemetry does not decide security authority.
